title: Who's left without a partner?
_map: Pairs and odd ones out (Y2). Big idea: even numbers split into pairs; odd numbers always leave one over. Is odd + odd odd or even? Test it and make a rule.
_story: Steve's sheep go on a walk in pairs, holding hooves. Some walks leave one sheep sad and alone. He tests numbers like a scientist, names even and odd, then runs an experiment: what happens when two odd groups meet?
_stepChain: counting → pairs → some numbers make only pairs → some leave one over → even → odd → predict odd + odd → test with sheep → rule

talk.ask: What's the difference between an even number and an odd number?
talk.goodAnswer: even numbers make pairs with none left over; odd numbers always have one left over.

talk.ask: Why is odd + odd always even?
talk.goodAnswer: each odd group has one left over, and the two left-over ones pair up with each other.

handsOn: Grab a handful of Lego bricks and pair them up. Odd or even? Grab another handful, put both together, and check again. Can you find an odd + odd that isn't even?

narration.speaker: steve
narration.text: My sheep love going for walks, two by two, side by side. Clip clop! But sometimes one sheep has nobody to walk with. Look how sad it is!
Let's be scientists! Pick how many sheep go for a walk, then tap the hammer. Does everyone get a partner? Try lots of numbers!
Some numbers make pairs with nobody left out. 2, 4, 6, 8, 10. Everyone has a friend! Numbers like those are called even.
Other numbers always leave one sheep on its own. 1, 3, 5, 7, 9. Poor lonely sheep! Numbers like those are called odd.

narration.speaker: steve
narration.text: Experiment time! 3 sheep meet 5 sheep. 3 is odd. 5 is odd. So I think together they'll make an even bigger odd group! Right?

question.prompt: What do you think? Odd or even together?
question.reveal: Even! 3 and 5 make 8. Each group had one lonely sheep. And the two lonely sheep became best friends! A new pair!

narration.speaker: steve
narration.text: Was that a lucky accident? Let's test it again! 7 sheep meet 9 sheep.

question.onRight: Yes! The two lonely sheep make a pair, so it's even again!

0.mistake: hasn't yet connected the two left-over sheep pairing up
0.hint: 7 has one sheep left over. 9 has one sheep left over. What can those two do together?
0.say: 7 has one lonely sheep. So does 9! Those two can walk together as a new pair. 7 and 9 make 16, and 16 is even!

question.reveal: 16 sheep, all in pairs! Odd and odd always make even.

rule.text: Even makes pairs. Odd has one left over.
rule.ask: What makes a number odd? And what does odd plus odd make? Say it out loud! Then tap the eye.
rule.spoken: Even numbers make pairs with none left over. Odd numbers always have one left over. And odd plus odd is always even.

bonus.prompt: Bonus! What about odd plus even? Guess, then test it with Lego!
bonus.reveal: Odd! The even group is all pairs. But the odd group still has its one lonely sheep.
